मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु ।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे ॥

texts.body:
manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru ।
māmevaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo'si me ॥

మన్మనా భవ మద్భక్తో మద్యాజీ మాం నమస్కురు ।
మామేవైష్యసి సత్యం తే ప్రతిజానే ప్రియోఽసి మే ॥
Merge thy mind in Me, be my devotee, sacrifice to Me, prostrate thyself before Me, thou shalt come even to Me. I pledge thee My troth; thou art dear to Me.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज ।
अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः ॥

texts.body:
sarvadharmānparityajya māmekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja ।
ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ ॥

సర్వధర్మాన్పరిత్యజ్య మామేకం శరణం వ్రజ ।
అహం త్వా సర్వపాపేభ్యో మోక్షయిష్యామి మా శుచః ॥
Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं ते नातपस्काय नाभक्ताय कदाचन ।
न चाशुश्रूषवे वाच्यं न च मां योऽभ्यसूयति ॥

texts.body:
idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadācana ।
na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo'bhyasūyati ॥

ఇదం తే నాతపస్కాయ నాభక్తాయ కదాచన ।
న చాశుశ్రూషవే వాచ్యం న చ మాం యోఽభ్యసూయతి ॥
Never is this to be spoken by thee to anyone who is without asceticism, nor without devotion, nor to one who desireth not to listen, nor yet to him who speaketh evil of Me.

verses.sanskrit:
य इमं परमं गुह्यं मद्भक्तेष्वभिधास्यति ।
भक्तिं मयि परां कृत्वा मामेवैष्यत्यसंशयः ॥

texts.body:
ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣvabhidhāsyati ।
bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ ॥

య ఇమం పరమం గుహ్యం మద్భక్తేష్వభిధాస్యతి ।
భక్తిం మయి పరాం కృత్వా మామేవైష్యత్యసంశయః ॥
He who shall declare this supreme secret among My devotees, having shown the highest devotion for Me, without doubt he shall come to Me.

verses.sanskrit:
न च तस्मान्मनुष्येषु कश्चिन्मे प्रियकृत्तमः ।
भविता न च मे तस्मादन्यः प्रियतरो भुवि ॥

texts.body:
na ca tasmānmanuṣyeṣu kaścinme priyakṛttamaḥ ।
bhavitā na ca me tasmādanyaḥ priyataro bhuvi ॥

న చ తస్మాన్మనుష్యేషు కశ్చిన్మే ప్రియకృత్తమః ।
భవితా న చ మే తస్మాదన్యః ప్రియతరో భువి ॥
Nor is there any among men who performeth dearer service to Me than he, nor any other shall be more beloved by Me on earth than he.

verses.sanskrit:
अध्येष्यते च य इमं धर्म्यं संवादमावयोः ।
ज्ञानयज्ञेन तेनाहमिष्टः स्यामिति मे मतिः ॥

texts.body:
adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādamāvayoḥ ।
jñānayajñena tenāhamiṣṭaḥ syāmiti me matiḥ ॥

అధ్యేష్యతే చ య ఇమం ధర్మ్యం సంవాదమావయోః ।
జ్ఞానయజ్ఞేన తేనాహమిష్టః స్యామితి మే మతిః ॥
And he who shall study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall be worshipped with the sacrifice of wisdom. Such is My mind.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाननसूयश्च शृणुयादपि यो नरः ।
सोऽपि मुक्तः शुभाँल्लोकान्प्राप्नुयात्पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥

texts.body:
śraddhāvānanasūyaśca śṛṇuyādapi yo naraḥ ।
so'pi muktaḥ śubhā~llokānprāpnuyātpuṇyakarmaṇām ॥

శ్రద్ధావాననసూయశ్చ శృణుయాదపి యో నరః ।
సోఽపి ముక్తః శుభాఁల్లోకాన్ప్రాప్నుయాత్పుణ్యకర్మణామ్ ॥
The man also who, full of faith, merely heareth it unreviling, even he, freed from evil, obtaineth the radiant worlds of the righteous.

verses.sanskrit:
कच्चिदेतच्छ्रुतं पार्थ त्वयैकाग्रेण चेतसा ।
कच्चिदज्ञानसंमोहः प्रनष्टस्ते धनञ्जय ॥

texts.body:
kaccidetacchrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā ।
kaccidajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭaste dhanañjaya ॥

కచ్చిదేతచ్ఛ్రుతం పార్థ త్వయైకాగ్రేణ చేతసా ।
కచ్చిదజ్ఞానసంమోహః ప్రనష్టస్తే ధనఞ్జయ ॥
Hath this been heard, O son of Prithâ, with one-pointed mind? Has thy delusion, caused by unwisdom, been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?

verses.speaker: arjuna
verses.sanskrit:
नष्टो मोहः स्मृतिर्लब्धा त्वत्प्रसादान्मयाच्युत ।
स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव ॥

texts.body:
naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtirlabdhā tvatprasādānmayācyuta ।
sthito'smi gatasandehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava ॥

నష్టో మోహః స్మృతిర్లబ్ధా త్వత్ప్రసాదాన్మయాచ్యుత ।
స్థితోఽస్మి గతసన్దేహః కరిష్యే వచనం తవ ॥
Destroyed is my delusion. I have gained knowledge through Thy grace, O Immutable one. I am firm, my doubts have fled away. I will do according to Thy word.

verses.speaker: sanjaya
verses.sanskrit:
इत्यहं वासुदेवस्य पार्थस्य च महात्मनः ।
संवादमिममश्रौषमद्भुतं रोमहर्षणम् ॥

texts.body:
ityahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ ।
saṃvādamimamaśrauṣamadbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam ॥

ఇత్యహం వాసుదేవస్య పార్థస్య చ మహాత్మనః ।
సంవాదమిమమశ్రౌషమద్భుతం రోమహర్షణమ్ ॥
I heard this marvellous dialogue of Vâsudeva, and of the great-souled Partha, causing my hair to stand on end.

verses.sanskrit:
व्यासप्रसादाच्छ्रुतवानेतद्गुह्यमहं परम् ।
योगं योगेश्वरात्कृष्णात्साक्षात्कथयतः स्वयम् ॥

texts.body:
vyāsaprasādācchrutavānetadguhyamahaṃ param ।
yogaṃ yogeśvarātkṛṣṇātsākṣātkathayataḥ svayam ॥

వ్యాసప్రసాదాచ్ఛ్రుతవానేతద్గుహ్యమహం పరమ్ ।
యోగం యోగేశ్వరాత్కృష్ణాత్సాక్షాత్కథయతః స్వయమ్ ॥
By the favour of Vyâsa I listened to this secret and supreme yoga from the Lord of Yoga, Krishna Himself, speaking before mine eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
राजन्संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य संवादमिममद्भुतम् ।
केशवार्जुनयोः पुण्यं हृष्यामि च मुहुर्मुहुः ॥

texts.body:
rājansaṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādamimamadbhutam ।
keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhurmuhuḥ ॥

రాజన్సంస్మృత్య సంస్మృత్య సంవాదమిమమద్భుతమ్ ।
కేశవార్జునయోః పుణ్యం హృష్యామి చ ముహుర్ముహుః ॥
O King, remembering, remembering this marvellous and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्च संस्मृत्य संस्मृत्य रूपमत्यद्भुतं हरेः ।
विस्मयो मे महान् राजन् हृष्यामि च पुनः पुनः ॥

texts.body:
tacca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpamatyadbhutaṃ hareḥ ।
vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ ॥

తచ్చ సంస్మృత్య సంస్మృత్య రూపమత్యద్భుతం హరేః ।
విస్మయో మే మహాన్ రాజన్ హృష్యామి చ పునః పునః ॥
Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः ।
तत्र श्रीर्विजयो भूतिर्ध्रुवा नीतिर्मतिर्मम ॥

texts.body:
yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ ।
tatra śrīrvijayo bhūtirdhruvā nītirmatirmama ॥

యత్ర యోగేశ్వరః కృష్ణో యత్ర పార్థో ధనుర్ధరః ।
తత్ర శ్రీర్విజయో భూతిర్ధ్రువా నీతిర్మతిర్మమ ॥
Wherever is Krishna, Yoga's Lord, wherever is Pârtha, the archer, assured are there prosperity, victory and happiness. So I think.

concepts.definition_en: Anger and how it arises from frustrated desire and clouds judgement.
Craving and selfish desire, which the Gita calls the enemy of wisdom.
Greed for more, named with desire and anger as a gate to ruin.
Fear, and the fearlessness of one whose mind is steady.
Agitation, worry and distress of mind, and the calm that is free of them.
Grief over loss, which Krishna answers by teaching what is permanent.
Arjuna's collapse of will and confusion about what is right, where the teaching begins.
Confusion that hides the truth, and the clarity that ends it.
Doubt, the doubting mind, and doubt cut by knowledge.
The ego that says "I am the doer", and the pride and hypocrisy it feeds.
Aversion, hatred and envy, and the freedom from them.
Clinging to things, people and outcomes, and acting without that clinging.
The fruits of action, to which you have no claim, and working without craving them.
Staying even-minded in success and failure, praise and blame, pleasure and pain.
The person of steady wisdom: how they speak, sit and walk, untouched by craving and fear.
The restless, wind-like mind, and how practice and detachment steady it.
Steady, repeated practice, the way the mind is trained.
Mastery of the senses, which pull the mind toward their objects.
How to sit, steady the mind and meditate, as taught in chapter 6.
Inner peace, which comes to one free of craving.
Kinds of happiness, the lasting joy within, and contentment.
Pain and suffering, why they pass, and the end of sorrow.
Why one must act, how to act without bondage, and action versus inaction.
The yoga of action: work done as an offering, without selfish motive.
One's own duty and nature, better done imperfectly than another's done well.
Righteousness, its decline, and the divine coming to restore it.
Why and when the Lord takes birth, to protect the good and restore dharma.
True renunciation is giving up the fruit and the selfish motive, not action itself.
Sloth, heedlessness and excess sleep, the marks of tamas.
Sattva, rajas and tamas, the three qualities of nature that bind and drive us.
Prakṛti, the material nature that acts, and each person's inborn nature.
The qualities that free us (fearlessness, purity, kindness) and those that bind (hypocrisy, arrogance, cruelty).
Kindness, friendliness and compassion toward all beings, without hatred.
Truthful, straightforward speech and conduct.
Forbearance, forgiveness and endurance through hardship.
Purity of body, mind and food, and what purifies.
Food that suits each temperament, and moderation in eating and sleep.
You are your own friend and your own enemy: raise yourself by yourself.
Acting for the welfare of the world; others follow what the best people do.
Arjuna's anguish over fighting his own family and teachers.
The battle of Kurukṣetra and the question of fighting a righteous war.
Honour and dishonour, praise and blame, and staying the same in both.
Giving, austerity and sacrifice, done in the sattvic way, are not to be abandoned.
Wrongdoing, its consequences, and how even the worst can be freed by knowledge and devotion.
Spiritual knowledge, the greatest purifier, and how to gain it.
Approaching a teacher with humility, questions and service.
Faith, which shapes a person ("as one's faith is, so one is"), and its three kinds.
The eternal Self that is never born and never dies, distinct from the body.
The body as the field, and the knower of the field who is not the body.
Death as changing worn-out clothes, rebirth, and what one remembers at the end.
Freedom from the cycle of birth and death, peace in Brahman, the supreme goal.
The Supreme Lord, the highest person, source and support of all.
The Lord dwelling in the heart of every being, and seeing the One in all.
Arjuna's vision of the Lord's cosmic form in chapter 11.
"Among X, I am Y": how the Lord is seen in whatever is excellent.
The cycles of creation and dissolution, the day of Brahmā, and nature as the womb.
What the Gita means by yoga: evenness of mind, skill in action, and freedom from union with pain.
The most secret, royal knowledge the Lord reveals to the devoted.
Loving devotion to the Lord, the path open to everyone.
The devotee dear to the Lord: without hatred, friendly, compassionate, the same in honour and dishonour.
Taking refuge in the Lord, who promises to free you from all sin and fear.
Offering everything you do, eat and give to the Lord: even a leaf, a flower, water.
Action done as sacrifice, which sustains the world and does not bind.
How people worship, the worship of other gods, and remembering the Lord.
